title: Alex Motor Imagery dataset
description: EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing cue-based motor imagery of the right hand, feet, and rest, with 20 trials per class. The data were collected for the PhD thesis of A. Barachant on robust control of an effector through an asynchronous EEG brain-machine interface, and correspond to Step B (cue-based imagery without feedback) of the Brain Switch campaign. They are intended for familiarization and algorithm development, including Riemannian geometry and CSP-based classification.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 16 active electrodes with a g.tec g.USBamp amplifier, referenced to the earlobe, in standard office conditions. Subjects imagined right hand movement, foot movement, or rest following visual cues lasting 3 seconds, with 20 trials per class and no feedback. Acquisition used Matlab/Simulink with g.tec drivers.
